articleSummary: Sporothrix brasiliensis, a zoonotic fungus transmitted from cats, originated in Brazil and has raised alarms across Uruguay and much of South America. The Uruguayan Institute of Hygiene confirmed cases in Maldonado and Rocha, signaling a shift in the regional epidemiology and prompting reinforced surveillance. The World Health Organization notes that in South American areas affected by this species—primarily Brazil—more than 11,000 human cases have been reported in the past decade. Transmission occurs through direct contact with infected cats, especially strays or animals with visible lesions. In felines, facial, muzzle, and paw ulcers are common and lesions with crusts facilitate transmission via scratches or bites to humans. In people, infections begin as skin and subcutaneous nodules, often along lymphatic channels; most are cutaneous but lymph nodes can be involved, requiring prolonged therapy. Early medical evaluation improves prognosis. Sporothrix brasiliensis is thermally dimorphic: filamentous at 25°C and yeast-like at 37°C.

The bacteria thrive in anaerobic, sealed or naturally fermented environments. Common sources include fermented fish, salted or cured fish, other fermented meats, homemade canned foods, pâté, sausages, smoked meats, and pickled vegetables produced without hygiene. articleHeadline: Leptospirosis cases have risen sharply in state over last five years
articleSummary: Leptospirosis cases in Karnataka have risen sharply, with over 16,000 infections in the past five years and about 30 deaths; 2025 recorded 6,525 cases and 19 deaths. Annual counts: 2020—544; 2021—906; 2022—3,174; 2023—5,404; 2024—5,088. Transmission occurs via water or soil contaminated with urine from infected animals, especially rodents; higher risk among agricultural, sanitation, and waste-disposal workers. Early symptoms manifest 2–14 days after exposure and include fever, severe headache, body pains (legs/back), chills, vomiting, fatigue, red eyes, and abdominal discomfort; without treatment, progression can cause kidney failure, liver damage/jaundice, breathing problems, lung infections, meningitis, and internal bleeding. Preventive measures during monsoon/flooding: avoid walking barefoot in contaminated water, wear protective boots and gloves for at-risk work, maintain hygiene, wash hands/feet, cover wounds, and control rodents plus ensure clean drinking water. Diagnosis relies on IgM ELISA screening, with MAT as confirmatory testing; PCR detects bacterial DNA early. Timely medical consultation improves outcomes.

articleHeadline: Here's what experts have to say about the new mpox variant that was detected in Toronto
articleSummary: Two travel-related mpox cases in Toronto involve a newly detected mpox clade Ib variant—the city's first. Mpox spreads through close, intimate or sexual contact, via infected lesions, skin blisters, bodily fluids, contaminated materials, or bites from animals, and LGBTQ2S+ men are most commonly affected. Classic skin lesions or rashes, sometimes in the mouth or genital region, with flu-like symptoms, are typical. The previously dominant clade in Toronto since 2022 has been IIb; clade I originated in eastern DRC and may be more severe, though evidence is uncertain. Diagnostics and treatment are the same across clades. Imvamune vaccine is available in Toronto (two doses, 28 days apart) with post-exposure prophylaxis. Canada has at least 14 mpox cases this year; last year Toronto had 155; Canada's peak was 1,541 four years ago.

articleSummary: Mpox can spread at home through contaminated objects (fomites); the virus can survive on everyday items and porous materials, enabling indirect transmission from infected individuals with skin lesions. articleHeadline: Banned foods and drinks your grandparents loved - including one 800 times more likely to cause food poisoning
articleSummary: Raw milk, potassium bromate, and coumarin were common in earlier decades but are now banned or restricted due to safety concerns. Potassium bromate, once used to strengthen dough and whiten flour, is tied to carcinogenic risks (IARC Group 2B; EU Group 1B). Historical limits included 75 mg/kg (WHO/FDA in 1993); Japan 10 mg/kg; China 50 mg/kg. Several countries—UK, Australia, New Zealand, China, Brazil—have banned it entirely. Raw milk poses a high risk of foodborne pathogens such as Campylobacter jejuni and Listeria monocytogenes; studies show contamination in up to 13% of samples, with risk roughly 800 times higher than pasteurized milk, causing fever, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and severe outcomes including meningitis, septicemia, abortion, tuberculosis, or death. Coumarin, used for flavoring, was banned in the US in 1954 due to liver toxicity; pure coumarin is not allowed, though naturally occurring levels remain in some foods and flavorings from natural sources.

articleHeadline: Covid и "русский грипп": ученые обнаружили в пандемических вирусах ключ к разгадке
articleSummary: Covid pandemic claimed over 25 million lives and triggered long-term health effects. A new Cell study by researchers from three US states analyzed seven outbreaks (Ebola, Marburg, HIV-1, influenza A, SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2) and monkeypox to chart pre-pandemic mutations. They found no unusual pre-pandemic changes in most viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, supporting natural zoonotic spillover; the 2009 H1N1 swine flu in the US caused about 61 million cases, 274,304 hospitalizations, and 12,469 deaths, and acquired mutations after crossing to humans. The 1977 Russian flu showed pre-pandemic mutations reminiscent of lab-derived patterns, a possible exception. The study argues that once a virus enters humans, mutations accelerate. For SARS-CoV-2, adaptation to bats preceded spread, with transmission linked to the Wuhan market, aligning with WHO. Ongoing debates about origins aside, widespread zoonotic circulation could heighten future pandemic risk.
notes: 本記事は米国の研究者によるCell誌掲載の学術研究で、過去7つのアウトブレイク（エボラ、マールブルグ、HIV-1、インフルエンザA、SARS-CoV、MERS-CoV、SARS-CoV-2）とMpoxのパンデミック前変異を分析したもの。新規の感染症発生や拡大を報告するものではなく、過去のウイルスの起源に関する科学的知見の提供のみ。1977年ロシア風邪に実験室由来パターンの可能性を示唆する点は学術的関心事項だが、現在進行中の公衆衛生上の脅威ではない。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Chinese city with 10,528 people infected with brucellosis after the bacteria escaped from the laboratory.
articleHeadline: Cidade chinesa com 10.528 infetados com brucelose após bactéria escapar de laboratório
articleSummary: Brucellosis outbreak in Lanzhou, Gansu, northwest China, after Brucella bacteria escaped from a public Lanzhou Bio-pharmaceutical Unit for Animal Breeding involved in animal vaccine production. More than 10,500 people have contracted brucellosis; 79,357 residents were tested and 1,604 treated. Brucellosis is transmitted from cattle, sheep, or pigs and is not usually contagious between humans, though infections cause fever, headache, and joint pain. Authorities traced the release to 2019 when an expired disinfectant was used during vaccine production, leading to incomplete sterilization and emissions that spread to the Institute of Veterinary Research, infecting nearly 200 people in December 2019. The facility’s vaccine production authorization was withdrawn, and affected patients are to receive financial compensation.
notes: 2019年の事象（期限切れ消毒剤使用による不完全滅菌→排出ガス拡散）の続報。79,357人が検査され10,528人陽性、1,604人治療済。施設のワクチン製造許可は取消済、患者への補償も実施中。ヒト-ヒト感染は通常なし。バイオセーフティ管理の失敗による大規模曝露事例として、国際的な教訓となる重要事例。

articleSummary: Monkeypox in Brazil nears 150 cases in 2026, with 140 confirmed and nine suspected across 13 states and the Federal District (Amazonas, Ceará, Minas Gerais, Pará, Paraná, Rio de Janeiro, Rio Grande do Norte, Rondônia, Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, Sergipe, São Paulo, Tocantins, plus DF). São Paulo accounts for 93 cases. No deaths have been reported. Authorities say there is no emerging crisis; 2022 remains the peak year with about 10,000 cases. Experts note mpox is endemic in Brazil, with ongoing monthly/weekly cases and sustained viral circulation. Transmission is mainly via prolonged close contact, especially sexual contact among men who have sex with men and sex workers; symptoms include fever with lesions and sometimes severe anal pain. Incubation ranges from 5–14 days, up to 21. After Carnival a possible small case surge may occur, but overall cases are historically moderate and non-lethal, with emphasis on surveillance and infection-prevention around patients.
notes: ブラジルでは既に風土病化しており、月次・週次で継続的に症例が発生。2022年のピーク時と比較して現在の症例数（150例程度）は著しく少ない。主な感染経路は性的接触を含む密接な接触。カーニバル後の症例増加の可能性が言及されているが、歴史的には中等度で致死的ではない。サーベイランスと感染予防策の継続が推奨されているが、緊急対応を要する状況ではない。情報更新があれば再評価が望ましい。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Brazil records its first measles case in 2026 - SiteBarra
articleHeadline: Brasil registra primeiro caso de sarampo em 2026 - SiteBarra
articleSummary: Brazil confirms its first measles case in 2026: a six-month-old unvaccinated infant in São Paulo. The infection is imported from Bolivia, which has experienced a measles outbreak since 2025; the child traveled between December 25 and January 25, developed fever and rash on February 8, with laboratory confirmation on March 4. PAHO/WHO warned of a resurgence of measles in the Americas after five years of low transmission; Brazil, however, remains free of endemic circulation per OPAS. In 2025 Brazil reported 38 cases across the Distrito Federal and six states: 10 imported, 25 related to importation, 3 with undefined origin; 94.7% had no vaccination or unknown vaccination status. Measles is highly contagious; symptoms include high fever, red rash, dry cough, conjunctivitis, coryza, and malaise. Vaccination is most effective; Brazil’s program covers ages 12 months to 59 years, with adolescents and adults advised to start/complete. SUS provides free MMR and tetraviral vaccines.
notes: ブラジルは風土的流行のない状態を維持しているが、2025年に38例報告され、94.7%がワクチン未接種または接種状況不明。今回の症例は生後6カ月の未接種乳児で、ボリビアのアウトブレイクからの輸入例。PAHO/WHOが5年ぶりの米州での麻疹再燃を警告している背景があり、域内での監視強化が必要な状況。単発輸入症例のため現時点でPICKUPには至らないが、ワクチン接種率と二次感染の有無について続報を注視すべき。

articleSummary: TB patients may undertake Lebaran mudik; there is no prohibition, but precautions apply. Pulmonologist Dr. Herman, Sp.P, FISR, told Health Liputan6.com in Bogor that TB patients should wear masks when traveling, especially during the first two weeks when infectiousness is highest. After two weeks, transmission risk declines, yet masking is advised when meeting crowds; if the patient remains negative after two months, a sputum test should be repeated. If sputum is negative, the patient is no longer contagious and can resume normal activities without masks. He notes ongoing measles outbreaks context; TB is bacterial, measles viral. If a TB patient contracts measles, both conditions require treatment—TB with anti-TB drugs, measles with antiviral therapy—taken at different times to avoid stomach upset. articleSummary: Bangkok Remand Prison clarified on 14 March 2026 that detainee Nawat Liengwatthana, aka ‘Amp,’ a Section 112 defendant, is not ill with monkeypox or chickenpox. Detained since 2 July 2024, he was found on 7 March 2026 to have one inflamed wound on the left ankle and two red bumps on the right thigh, with mild local pain and no fever, prompting isolated observation. On 10 March 2026, prior to a court appearance, an on-duty physician concluded there was no evidence of monkeypox or chickenpox, allowing release from quarantine. On 11 March 2026, nurses re-evaluated, explained the condition, and continued daily wound care and medications at the prison hospital. The detainee understood the diagnosis, showed no anxiety, and monitoring continues by prison medical staff.
notes: これは刑務所内の単一被拘禁者に関する医療情報の訂正発表であり、実際の感染症イベントではない。医師による診察の結果、サル痘・水痘のいずれも否定されており、単なる皮膚の炎症と診断されている。疫学的意義はなく、公衆衛生対応の必要性もない。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Several parts of South America report a "sustained transmission" of yellow fever, according to PAHO.
articleHeadline: Varias partes de Sudamérica registran una "transmisión sostenida" de la fiebre amarilla, según la OPS
articleSummary: Yellow fever is experiencing sustained transmission across several parts of South America, per PAHO. In 2025, 346 confirmed cases and 143 deaths across seven countries: Bolivia (8/2), Brazil (120/48), Colombia (125/46), Ecuador (11/8), Peru (49/19), Venezuela (32/19); Guyana figures not specified. PAHO urges member states to strengthen epidemiological surveillance and boost vaccination campaigns in at-risk populations. The detection of cases near urban centers raises the risk of urban transmission, as the virus spreads between people via the Aedes aegypti mosquito, potentially driving rapid outbreaks. Vaccination and vector control measures are critical to curb spread. The report highlights the need to intensify vaccination campaigns in high-risk areas near urban centers to prevent urban amplification of transmission.
notes: 2025年の事例として7カ国で346確定例・143死亡（致命率41%）は極めて深刻。都市中心部近郊での症例検出により、ネッタイシマカ（Aedes aegypti）を介した都市型伝播への移行リスクが指摘されており、急速な流行拡大の可能性がある。PAHOが加盟国に疫学サーベイランス強化とワクチンキャンペーン拡充を緊急要請している点からも、国際的支援の必要性が高い。複数国にまたがる持続伝播は地域的な公衆衛生危機として扱うべき。
